title: A morphism of affine schemes is a closed immersion exactly when it lifts against every injective ring map

standard_prerequisites.name: Explicit prerequisite boundary
standard_prerequisites.reference: Closed immersions of affine schemes, surjectivity of ring maps, anti-equivalence between rings and affine schemes; no cited result replaces the retained argument
standard_prerequisites.use: The dictionary between closed immersions of affine schemes and surjective ring maps, pullback squares of spectra, and the Yoneda/anti-equivalence bookkeeping. All are standard; both directions of the criterion are retained.

core_obligations: From surjectivity of phi, construct the lift S -> A by choosing a preimage and proving well-definedness from injectivity of psi and commutativity of the square.
For the converse, build the test square with phi(R) as the test ring, apply the lifting hypothesis, and deduce that the inclusion phi(R) -> S is an isomorphism, hence phi is surjective.

proof_roadmap.step: Reduce the criterion to surjectivity of the induced ring map phi : R -> S, then prove the forward direction by the explicit lift s maps to alpha(r).
Assume phi has lifts against every injective ring map, form the square with phi(R) as test ring, and conclude surjectivity of phi.

spans.label: converse direction via the subring test

difficulty_reason: The criterion converts a surjectivity statement about a ring map into a lifting property against all injective ring maps, and the two directions need different work. Surjective phi gives a lift by the tautological formula s maps to alpha(r) for any r with phi(r) = s, whose well-definedness uses injectivity of psi together with commutativity of the square, followed by the spectrum anti-equivalence. The converse manufactures the test square from phi itself, using the subring phi(R) of S as the test ring, and the existence of the lift forces the inclusion phi(R) -> S to be an isomorphism. The whole content is in choosing the right test ring rather than in executing a standard limit argument. Retained author proof at lines 23509-23544.
